description: Oregon — "Beaver State" — entered the Union 1859 (33rd). Its capital is Salem and its largest city is Portland. Chinook; Oregon Trail. This database tells the state's story: from its first peoples through statehood to the modern era, plus the famous sons and daughters, the industries, and the facts every resident should know.

title: Statehood
description: Oregon achieved statehood 1859 (33rd). The road to statehood ran through territorial government, population thresholds, and a congressional enabling act — the standard American path. Statehood 1859. Statehood Day is still celebrated, and the admission order gives Oregon its number among the states.

description: The statehood story of Oregon: settlement, territorial organization, the push for admission, and finally the star on the flag. Timber to tech (Silicon Forest). Every state's admission reflected the national politics of its era — Oregon's story is no exception, and it explains much about the state's character today.

title: Capital: Salem
d: Salem is the capital of Oregon.
definition: Salem is the capital of Oregon.
description: Salem has been the seat of Oregon government, home to the capitol building, the supreme court, and the legislature. Capitals are often not the biggest city — Oregon's largest is Portland — chosen instead for geography or politics. Visit the capitol: the building itself tells the state's story in stone.

title: Nickname: Beaver State
description: The nickname "Beaver State" captures how Oregon sees itself — and how America sees it. The Oregon Trail brought settlers west. State nicknames come from history, geography, or industry, and they appear on license plates, tourism campaigns, and sports teams. The motto goes deeper: "Alis volat propriis (She flies with her own wings)."

title: Motto: Alis volat propriis (She flies with her own wings)
t: Motto: Alis volat propriis (She flies with her own wings)
d: The state motto of Oregon is "Alis volat propriis (She flies with her own wings)."
definition: The state motto of Oregon is "Alis volat propriis (She flies with her own wings)."
description: The motto "Alis volat propriis (She flies with her own wings)" is Oregon's official creed, adopted by the legislature and carried on the state seal. Seal with beaver and ship on blue. Mottos distill a state's ideals into a phrase — learn it, and you understand what the state aspires to be.
